column3: NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1. “Righteousness” is rendered “a just cause,” and NASB supplies “which is … from” in the last clause.
Close to the Hebrew; “may Your eyes see uprightness” is rendered “Let Your eyes look with equity.”
Close to the Hebrew; “You visited at night” is rendered “You have visited me by night,” and “You will not find” as “You find nothing.”
“I have watched the paths of the violent” is rendered “I have kept from the paths of the violent,” with “from” supplied.
Close to the Hebrew; “in Your tracks” is rendered “to Your paths.”
“Make wonderful Your covenant loyalties” is rendered “Wondrously show Your lovingkindness”; NASB joins “at Your right hand” to “take refuge” and supplies “against them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the pupil of the daughter of an eye” is rendered “the apple of the eye.”
Close to the Hebrew; “enemies in soul” is rendered “My deadly enemies.”
“Their fat they have closed” is rendered “They have closed their unfeeling heart,” and “their mouth” as “With their mouth.”
Close to the Hebrew; “his likeness is like a lion” is rendered “He is like a lion.”
The Hebrew is difficult; “Your treasured thing” is rendered “Your treasure,” and “they are satisfied with sons” as “satisfied with children.” The meaning is uncertain.
